title: Angles in Parallel Lines & Triangles
description: Learn about Angles in Parallel Lines and Triangles for Grade 7: corresponding angles, alternate interior angles, triangle angle sum and exterior angle theorem.

topics.title: Parallel Lines Angle Relationships
topics.concept:
When a transversal crosses two parallel lines, 8 angles are formed with special relationships:

Angle PairRelationshipExamples
CorrespondingEQUAL1=5, 2=6, 3=7, 4=8
Alternate InteriorEQUAL3=6, 4=5
Alternate ExteriorEQUAL1=8, 2=7
Consecutive InteriorSum = 180 degrees3+5=180, 4+6=180

Consecutive interior angles are also called co-interior or same-side interior angles.

Corresponding (equal): 1=5, 2=6, 3=7, 4=8
Alternate interior (equal): 3=6, 4=5
Alternate exterior (equal): 1=8, 2=7
Consecutive interior (sum 180): 3+5=180, 4+6=180

examples.problem: If angle 1 = 70 degrees, find angles 5, 3, and 6.
examples.solution: Angle 5 = 70 deg (corresponding). Angle 3 = 70 deg (vertical to angle 1). Angle 6 = 110 deg (consecutive interior: 70+110=180).

examples.problem: Alternate interior angles are (3x+20) and (5x-40) degrees. Find x.
examples.solution: Alternate interior angles are equal: 3x+20 = 5x-40 => 60 = 2x => x = 30.

recap: Consecutive interior angles SUM to 180 degrees

topics.title: Triangle Angle Sum & Exterior Angle Theorem
topics.concept:
Triangle Angle Sum Theorem: The three interior angles of any triangle always add up to 180 degrees.

Angle A + Angle B + Angle C = 180 degrees

Exterior Angle Theorem: An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two non-adjacent (remote) interior angles.

This is because the exterior angle and its adjacent interior angle form a straight line (180 deg), and that interior angle plus the other two = 180 deg.

    A____50____B
          70

  50 + 60 + 70 = 180 degrees

EXTERIOR ANGLE THEOREM:

    C
    /\
   /  \
  A----B----D
           ^
   Exterior angle at D = angle A + angle C

examples.problem: Triangle has angles 45 and 75 degrees. Find the third angle.
In a triangle, one angle is twice another, and the third angle is 30 degrees. Find all angles.
examples.solution: Let angles be x, 2x, 30. x + 2x + 30 = 180 => 3x = 150 => x = 50. Angles: 50, 100, 30 degrees.

examples.problem: An exterior angle of a triangle is 130 degrees, and one remote interior angle is 55 degrees. Find the other remote interior angle.

recap: Sum of interior angles in any triangle = 180 degrees
Exterior angle = sum of the two non-adjacent interior angles
Can use algebra to find missing angles
The largest angle is always opposite the longest side

online.title: Online Test — Chapter 8: Angles in Parallel Lines & Triangles

questions.q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. If one corresponding angle = 75 degrees, what is the other corresponding angle?
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles are equal when lines are parallel, so 75 degrees.

questions.q: Alternate interior angles measure (4x+10) and (6x-30) degrees. Find x.
questions.explanation: Alternate interior angles are equal: 4x+10 = 6x-30 => 40 = 2x => x = 20

questions.q: A triangle has angles 40 and 60 degrees. Find the third angle.
An exterior angle of a triangle = 110 degrees. The two remote interior angles are in ratio 5:6. Find the smaller remote interior angle.
In a triangle, angles are x, 2x, and 3x degrees. Find the largest angle.
Consecutive interior angles measure 125 and 55 degrees. Are the lines parallel?
questions.explanation: 125 + 55 = 180 degrees. Consecutive interior angles summing to 180 means lines are parallel.

questions.q: A transversal crosses two parallel lines. One angle formed is 120 degrees. What is its alternate interior angle?
questions.explanation: Alternate interior angles are equal when lines are parallel, so the angle is also 120 degrees.

questions.q: Triangle has angles (x+20), (2x+10), and 60 degrees. Find x.
An exterior angle is 135 degrees and one remote interior angle is 45 degrees. Find the other remote interior angle.
questions.explanation: Exterior angle = sum of remote interior angles. Other angle = 135 - 45 = 90 degrees.

questions.q: An isosceles triangle has a vertex angle of 40 degrees. Find each base angle.
questions.explanation: Base angles are equal. 40 + 2b = 180 => 2b = 140 => b = 70 degrees each.

questions.q: In triangle ABC, angle A = 50 degrees and angle B = 70 degrees. Find the exterior angle at vertex C.
questions.explanation: Exterior angle at C = angle A + angle B = 50 + 70 = 120 degrees.

questions.q: In a parallelogram, one angle is 65 degrees. Find the largest angle.
questions.explanation: Consecutive angles in a parallelogram are supplementary: 180 - 65 = 115 degrees is the largest.

questions.q: Two parallel lines cut by a transversal. One angle = (7x-20) degrees and its corresponding angle = (3x+60) degrees. Find x.
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles are equal: 7x-20 = 3x+60 => 4x = 80 => x = 20. Angle = 7(20)-20 = 120 degrees.

questions.q: Triangle PQR has angles 2x, 3x, and 5x degrees. Classify the triangle by its angles.
questions.explanation: 2x+3x+5x=180 => 10x=180 => x=18. Angles: 36, 54, 90 degrees. Since one angle is 90, it is a right triangle.

questions.q: The exterior angle at vertex A of triangle ABC is 150 degrees. If angle B : angle C = 2:3, find angle B.
questions.explanation: Angle B + angle C = 150. Ratio 2:3 => 2k+3k=150 => k=30. Angle B = 60 degrees.

questions.q: Two parallel lines L1 and L2 are cut by a transversal. One angle at L1 is 70 degrees. Find the consecutive interior angle at L2.
questions.explanation: Consecutive interior angles are supplementary (sum to 180): 180 - 70 = 110 degrees.
